USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Anatomic site of disease

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An adult develops severe odynophagia and a muffled voice despite a relatively unremarkable visible oropharynx. Flexible examination by an experienced clinician reveals swollen tissue surrounding the laryngeal inlet. Which region is primarily affected?

  1. Supraglottic structures including the epiglottis
  2. Subglottic larynx below the vocal cords
  3. Peritonsillar tissues beside the palatine tonsil
  4. Retropharyngeal space behind the pharyngeal wall
  5. Distal tracheal mucosa below the larynx
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Supraglottic structures including the epiglottis

Epiglottitis is often termed supraglottitis because nearby supraglottic structures may also be inflamed.

Understanding the options

Supraglottic structures including the epiglottis
Epiglottitis is often termed supraglottitis because nearby supraglottic structures may also be inflamed.
Subglottic larynx below the vocal cords
This is the principal region narrowed in croup, not the described swelling around the laryngeal inlet.
Peritonsillar tissues beside the palatine tonsil
A peritonsillar process generally produces a visible unilateral oropharyngeal bulge.
Retropharyngeal space behind the pharyngeal wall
This is a deep-neck space rather than tissue surrounding the laryngeal inlet.
Distal tracheal mucosa below the larynx
Tracheitis is lower than the described supraglottic inflammation.
